questions.text: "I wish I ___ the answer to this question right now."
questions.hint: Wish + past simple = present impossible wish

questions.text: "If only she ___ that email — it caused so many problems."
questions.hint: If only + past perfect = past regret

questions.text: "I'd rather you ___ (not/tell) anyone about this conversation."
questions.hint: Would rather + different subject + past simple negative

questions.text: "It's high time they ___ a decision about the future."
questions.hint: It's (high) time + past simple

questions.text: "___ the results had been different, we would have continued the project." (Formal inverted)
questions.hint: Had + subject + pp = inverted past conditional

questions.text: "___ she to leave the company, the entire team would be affected." (Formal present hypothetical)
questions.hint: Were + subject + to-infinitive = formal inverted conditional

questions.text: "He speaks as if he ___ everything." (He doesn't know everything)
questions.hint: As if + past simple = unreal present comparison

questions.text: "I wish you ___ making that noise!" (Annoyance about current habit)
questions.hint: Wish + would = annoyance / request for change

questions.text: "___ you need additional information, please contact our office." (Formal polite condition)
questions.hint: Should + subject = formal inverted conditional

questions.text: "Supposing we ___ the budget — what would we prioritise?" (future hypothetical)
questions.hint: Supposing + past simple = present/future hypothetical

questions.text: What is the main difference between "I wish I had done X" and "I regret doing X"?
questions.hint: Key concept from Listening 3B / Reading 1

questions.text: "What if they ___ the problem earlier?" (= They didn't notice it — past hypothetical)
questions.hint: What if + past perfect = past hypothetical

questions.text: "___ I had listened to that advice, I would not be in this situation now." (Mixed conditional — formal inverted)
questions.hint: Had + subject + pp = inverted past conditional

questions.text: In the context of regret, "in hindsight" means…
opts: at the same time as the event
questions.hint: "In hindsight, everything is obvious"

questions.text: "We idealise the roads not taken" means…
opts: We imagine unchosen paths as better than they might have been
We regret every choice we make
We travel different roads as often as possible
questions.correct: We imagine unchosen paths as better than they might have been
questions.hint: From Listening 3 dialogue

questions.text: "She looked as though she ___ (just see) something terrible."
questions.hint: As though + past perfect for unreal past comparison

questions.text: "It would ___ preferable to consult the team first." (Expresses regret without assigning blame)
questions.hint: "It would have been preferable to…" = regret without blame

questions.text: "___ you could change one decision in your life — what would it be?" (Hypothetical invitation)
questions.hint: "Imagine" introduces hypothetical scenarios

questions.text: "I'd rather ___ (stay) at home than go to the party tonight." (Same subject preference)
questions.hint: Would rather + bare infinitive (same subject)

questions.text: A "counterfactual" statement describes…
opts: What might have happened under different conditions
What will happen in the future
questions.correct: What might have happened under different conditions
questions.hint: Para 1 of Reading 1: "contrary to fact"

questions.text: "If only I ___ harder at school — things would be different." (Past regret, strong emotion)
questions.hint: If only + past perfect = intense past regret

questions.text: The ability to make something seem better than it is = to ___ it.
questions.hint: "We idealise the roads not taken"

questions.text: Which is the most formal way to express a past conditional?
opts: If they had checked, the error would have been caught.
Had they checked, the error would have been caught.
questions.correct: Had they checked, the error would have been caught.
questions.hint: Inverted conditional = most formal register

questions.text: "I'd rather you hadn't mentioned that" uses the past perfect to express a preference about the past.
questions.hint: Would rather + subject + past perfect = past preference/regret

questions.text: If something is "evasive," it…
opts: Avoids a direct answer or acknowledgement
questions.correct: Avoids a direct answer or acknowledgement
questions.hint: From Listening 3B lecture
